catalyst.action: UPDATE to the position opened 2026-09-24 at 39.60 — hold, levels unchanged. Do not add before the minutes; the position is already on.

thesis: This is an update to a live short, not a new idea: the position was opened 2026-09-24 at 39.60 and sits at 39.97, 0.6% against. What changed is the driver got stronger, not the price — the 10y printed 5.315% Monday, a fresh 52-week high and the highest in over two decades, and the move is term premium and issuance rather than Fed expectations, which is the version of a rate rise a bond-proxy sector cannot grow its way out of. Levels are deliberately left exactly where they were.
key_risk: Utilities are no longer a pure bond proxy — the AI-datacenter power bid is real, and it showed on Monday with CEG +3.9% and VST +3.5%. If that bid broadens from the independent power producers into the regulated names XLU is mostly made of, the rate link breaks and the short is wrong for a reason that has nothing to do with the curve.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the short end is already pricing cuts after a weak payrolls print with 60k of downward revisions, and a dovish set of minutes tomorrow could pull the whole curve down and squeeze this. Answered on the tape rather than asserted: Friday was exactly that weak print, and the 10y still sat at ~5.25% into Monday and then made a new high. The long end has already declined to trade the labour data once.

catalyst.event: Thesis falsified — gold in a 21% drawdown while miners underperform the metal
catalyst.action: CLOSE the long opened 2026-09-26 at 91.20. Exit at market on the open; do not wait for the 85.40 stop 0.7% lower. This is an exit instruction, not a new short.

thesis: This closes an existing long rather than opening anything. The position was entered at 91.20 on 2026-09-26 for a gold-strength thesis, and gold has not cooperated: GLD is 379.55 against a range high of 481.31, a 21.1% drawdown, and sits only 4.5% above its range low. GDX itself is 17.3% off its high and below both its SMA20 of 93.06 and SMA50 of 91.68.
key_risk: Exiting 0.7% above the stop gives up the bounce if gold has bottomed here, and GDX did outperform GLD over six months (-6.82% vs -11.25%), so the miners are not uniformly weaker. If the long end reverses and real yields fall, this is sold at the low.
counter_argument: The strongest case for holding is that the stop is only 2.3% away, so the remaining risk is small and the option value of a bounce is free. It is not free: the one-month read has GDX -13.86% against GLD -7.48%, miners falling at nearly twice the metal rate. Operating leverage running backwards means the equity is discounting lower realised gold, and that is the signal to act on rather than wait out.

thesis: A $171.5B staple trading at 14.46x forward earnings on a 4.71% dividend yield, 24.9% off its high, because Frito-Lay North America volumes are shrinking. That is a fixable distribution-and-pricing problem rather than a broken franchise, and the fix is contracted: the company has committed in writing to at least 100bps of core operating margin expansion over FY2026-2028, a ~20% SKU reduction, three plant closures, capex under 5% of revenue and FCF conversion of at least 80%. Elliott holds roughly $4B and settled rather than fighting a proxy battle, which is what makes the commitment enforceable rather than aspirational.
key_risk: Relative strength says this is still falling, not bottoming: PEP is -19.83% over six months against XLP -1.96%, so it is losing badly to its own sector and not merely to an index that semis are carrying. Consensus EPS has been cut 5.24% in 90 days and the revision direction is deteriorating, so the 14.46x forward multiple is on a number that is still moving down. INVALIDATION, stated concretely: core operating margin fails to expand year-over-year in FY2026 as reported, or PFNA organic volume declines worsen for two more consecutive quarters, or the dividend increase promised for 2026 does not arrive. Any of those means the turnaround is not happening and the cheapness is a value trap.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that GLP-1 drugs are a permanent structural hit to salty-snack demand, which would make every multiple here a trap rather than a discount. I cannot dismiss that, and I am not pretending to: it is the reason the entry is a staged zone 6% below the market and the last third waits under 112 rather than being bought at the 52-week low today. What the bear case has to survive is a 4.71% yield on a company guiding to 2-4% organic revenue growth and 5-7% core EPS growth for 2026 — the price is already paying for a good deal of the structural story.

catalyst.event: US federal money moving into nuclear capacity — DOE approved a ~$4.2B loan package on 2026-10-05 to uprate three Vistra nuclear plants on the PJM grid
catalyst.action: UPDATE to the position opened 2026-08-17 at 94.00 — hold, entry, target and stop all unchanged. Do not average down; the 82.5 stop is 5.7% away and is the risk control.

thesis: Update to a live position, down 7.0% from a 94.00 entry. What changed on Monday is that the nuclear build-out stopped being a narrative and became an appropriation: the DOE approved a roughly $4.2B loan package to uprate three Vistra nuclear plants serving PJM, which moved CCJ +2.69% to 87.47 on a day the long end was selling off. Uprates and restarts consume enriched fuel on a multi-year contract cycle, and Cameco sells the fuel regardless of which utility wins the datacenter contract.
key_risk: The chart does not support the story yet. CCJ is 35.3% off its 52-week high of 135.24 and below its SMA20 (91.50), SMA50 (94.61) and SMA200 (105.66) — a full downtrend, with the 52-week low at 77.70 only 11% below. One day of +2.69% on another company news is not a trend change, and the 135.0 target is the old high, which requires the whole de-rating to reverse.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that uranium equities already priced the nuclear renaissance in 2024-25 and the 35% de-rate is the market correctly marking down contract pricing that never materialised. The partial answer is that the DOE loan is capital actually committed to physical uprates rather than a letter of intent, and uprates raise fuel burn mechanically. What I cannot answer is the timing — that is why this stays a hold at an unchanged stop rather than an add.

thesis: Bitcoin has repaired a 31.6% drawdown and IBIT now trades at 48.56 above its SMA20 (46.18), SMA50 (42.21) and SMA200 (41.91) in that order, which is a reclaimed trend rather than a bounce. It has spent two weeks coiling in 46.71-49.39 while spot BTC ETFs took $241.09M of inflows in a third straight positive week, so the consolidation is absorbing supply rather than distributing. The relative strength is leadership: +34.33% over three months against SPY +3.63%.
key_risk: IBIT does not trade when bitcoin does. The underlying runs 24/7 and the fund opens Monday wherever the weekend left it, so the 46.15 stop can be gapped straight through rather than filled — the stop is a level, not a guarantee. A 2.5 ATR stop is sized for that, but a weekend liquidation is exactly the event it cannot absorb.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that bitcoin is simply high-beta risk appetite and the 10y at a two-decade high is the most hostile possible backdrop for a zero-yield asset. The evidence cuts the other way over the precise window in question: BTC is +34% on three months while yields were climbing to that two-decade high, and it beat gold — the other debasement asset — by roughly 34 points over the same stretch while GLD sits 21% off its high. Whatever is bidding bitcoin is not simple duration appetite, because duration was being sold throughout.

catalyst.action: Enter at market in 95.50-98.00; this is an at-market entry on reclaimed support, not a limit below the tape. Trim half at 108. thesis: The bear steepener that is marking down bank securities books does the opposite to a life insurer: MetLife discounts long-dated policy liabilities at the higher long rate while reinvesting float at the new yields, so the single largest force in this market is a tailwind here and a headwind three doors down. The market is not paying for it — 9.05x forward earnings against 18.57x trailing, with a $3.0B buyback authorised on 2026-08-05 retiring 4.9% of a $61.57B cap. MetLife went out of its way on 2026-09-24 to pre-announce at least $600M of Q3 variable investment income against roughly $1.6B of full-year guidance, which is 37.5% of the annual number in one quarter.
key_risk: Variable investment income is private equity, real estate, other funds and prepayment fees — the most mark-dependent line in the P&L, and the one the 8-K itself cautions is not indicative of future periods. If the same long-rate move that helps the liability side cracks commercial real estate marks, the pre-announced strength reverses into the exact line that drove it. Credit is the other side: unemployment at 4.2% and rising eventually shows up in the corporate bond portfolio.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that MET is simply a financial, financials are being sold hard (XLF -7.99% in a month, BAC -17% off its high), and a single name cannot hold out against its sector. The six-month record is the answer and it is measured, not asserted: MET +36.37% against XLF +8.02%, a 28-point spread built over exactly the period the sector de-rated, with revision direction improving while the banks deteriorated and zero sell ratings among 24 analysts. It has already not been dragged down, through two quarters of the thing the objection predicts.

catalyst.event: Mortgage rates at a two-decade high have falsified the recovery thesis — 30-year fixed 7.28% as of 2026-10-01, up from 7.03% a week earlier
catalyst.action: CLOSE the long opened 2026-08-18 at 94.00. Exit at market. This is an exit instruction, not a new short — do not establish a short position in it.

thesis: This closes a losing long whose driver has moved decisively against it. LCI makes components for recreational vehicles — a financed, discretionary, big-ticket purchase and therefore the single most rate-sensitive thing a consumer buys — and the 30-year mortgage that proxies household borrowing costs went to 7.28% on 2026-10-01 from 7.03% the week before, following the 10y to a two-decade high. The stock is 48.3% off its high at 82.58 and sits 1.75% above its 52-week low of 81.16, below its SMA20, SMA50 and SMA200. It is making new lows rather than basing, and the position carries no stop, so the loss is currently unbounded.
key_risk: Selling 1.75% off a 52-week low is selling into the exact zone where a washed-out cyclical bottoms, and if the long end reverses this is the kind of name that rallies 30% before anyone updates a spreadsheet. Accepting an 11.9% loss here means forgoing that.
counter_argument: The strongest case for holding is that an RV-cycle trough is a real thing and the 138.00 target is a cycle-recovery number, not a fantasy. The problem is the arithmetic of waiting: 138.00 from 82.58 is a 67% advance that requires the rate environment to fully reverse, while the position has no stop and the housing data is still deteriorating on fetched numbers — existing home sales 3.98M in August against 4.06M in July, and NAR cutting its 2026 forecast from +14% to +4%. An unbounded position waiting on a 67% move against a worsening driver is not a hold, it is a hope.

evidence.detail: 82.58 is 48.3% below the 159.66 high and 1.75% above the 81.16 52-week low, with price below SMA20 87.33, SMA50 97.64 and SMA200 115.22 — a full downtrend making new lows
